## This week

You posted 23 videos this week. That is way more than last week's 13. But the numbers still came in lower. Your typical video this week landed around 683 views, while last week's typical video got about 1,608 views. Your best video was the one that starts with "This is coming from a girl that made $100,000 in her first six months doing UGC." It pulled in 2,810 views. Your weakest was the one that starts with "Number one, pick one to two niches. Beauty, tech, health." which only got 279 views. A few from this week, like the "I got scammed" video, are still too fresh to judge fairly.

## Is it how you film, or what you say?

Here is the catch. Every single video you posted this week was talking to camera. No voice over footage, no text on screen, nothing else. So this week can't tell us if format matters, because you didn't test anything else.

Looking at your whole library, format barely moves the needle at all. It is the weakest signal out of everything. What actually seems to matter more is your structure, like step by step or list style videos, and your topic, like how you got started. I don't have two versions of the same script filmed differently to compare side by side yet, so I can't give you a clean before and after. Right now, it looks like what you say and how you build the video matters more than which format you film it in.

## What is working

Your "how you got started" videos usually pull about one and a half times your normal views. You have posted 35 of those, so that is a real pattern.

Your "real money numbers" videos do even better, around four times your usual views. You have only posted 9 of those though, so keep an eye on it as it grows.

Videos that end by sending people to your link in bio are massive, about 17 times your normal views. You have only tried this 8 times, so it is promising but still early.

## Try this next week

Film a "how you got started" story using a clear step by step structure, since both of those do well on their own.

Try a "real money numbers" video that ends by pointing people to your link in bio, since both of those are your biggest hitters.

Take one script you already used, like the "$100,000 in six months" one, and film it again as voice over footage instead of talking to camera, so we can finally see if format changes anything.

best.md:
This video came in under what you'd normally expect, about 60% of your usual views. It's still tagged "best" because this topic and hook style usually pull in more than your typical video, so the format had real potential here.

Your opener, "This is coming from a girl that made $100,000 in her first six months doing UGC," is a strong stop-the-scroll line. But right after it, you jump straight into defining Canvas UGC instead of teasing what's coming. That first 3 seconds earns attention, but seconds 3 to 6 don't build a reason to keep watching, they just start the lesson.

After that opener, the video does keep giving value step by step, the contract, the Discord, the briefs, the posting schedule. That structure is good for holding people once they're in.

You had no call to action in the video itself, only in the caption. Next time, say the workshop invite out loud partway through, right after you deliver the first useful tip, not left for people to find in the caption.

worst.md:
This video did badly. You got 622 views, while a normal video of yours gets 4,019. That is way under your usual.

Your opening line was "In the next 30 seconds, I'm gonna explain how creators are making $50,000." That is a strong stakes hook, the kind that usually works great for you. In fact, videos with this hook style normally pull in about 14,100 views for you, so this one landed far below what this exact hook usually earns.

After the opening, the video did keep building. You explained the math step by step, $10k to $1,500, $100k to $15,000, which gives people a reason to keep watching and see how the numbers work.

There was no call to action in this video. Since you ended by teasing "next time," you could have instead asked people to follow so they don't miss that next video, or comment a word to get more info now.

Next time, add a clear call to action in the middle of the video, right after you explain the payout math, asking people to follow for the next part.
